links.note: Naming a value children learn in the family - this concept lists ahimsa, dana or giving, seva or service, and tyaga or sacrifice.
Dana glossed as giving - this concept's gloss.
Seva glossed as service - this concept's gloss.
Shalini's family preparing for the festival of Onam - this concept's setting. Already linked and correct.
Tenzing's mother making traditional fabrics and wood carvings in the handicraft cooperative - this concept's detail. Already linked and correct.
A group of connected people called a community - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
The town of Jhabua in Madhya Pradesh, where the Bhils planted trees and dug trenches - this concept's setting. Already linked and correct.
Shri Mahesh Sharma of the Shivganga movement honoured with the Padma Shri in 2019 for his work with the Bhil communities - this concept's closing line.
Kamal Parmar giving tuition from 5:30 to 9:30 pm and providing a free dinner - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
A jati, or a subdivision of it, often called a community - this concept's first example of the word's flexibility.
Tiruvalluvar's line that love and dharma are the flower and fruit of family life - this concept opens the chapter on it, before defining the family as the fundamental unit of society.
Interdependence among family members - this concept's opening sentence names it beside love, care and cooperation, and says the chapter will reuse the word of communities. Already linked and correct.
Parents being responsible for raising their children to become happy individuals and responsible members of society - this concept's sentence.
Acchamma, Shalini's grandmother and her father's mother - this concept names the relation. Already linked and correct.
Tenzing's grandfather helping with homework and taking him to the school bus stop - this concept's detail. Already linked and correct.
Residents Welfare Associations making rules about waste management, cleanliness of common areas and taking care of pets - this concept's list. Already linked and correct.
Communities agreeing over time on practices for the use of shared natural wealth such as water, grazing lands and forest produce - this concept's sentence.
A joint family with several generations - grandparents, parents, uncles and aunts, brothers, sisters and cousins - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
A nuclear family limited to a couple and their children, against the joint family's several generations - this concept's pair. Already linked and correct.

Why Indian languages have more kinship terms than English - this concept's observation, with bua, tau, tai, chacha, mausi, nana and nani as examples and Tamil distinguishing elder from younger siblings.
Cousins being only brothers and sisters, which emphasises the deep bonds among all the children in the family - this concept's conclusion from the missing word.
The responsibilities of parents towards their children - this concept states them as raising children to become happy individuals and responsible members of society.
Tyaga or sacrifice as a family value - this concept glosses it and adds that individuals in the family often give up their own needs to take care of the family's.
Acchamma explaining that this is how families support each other and share what they have - this concept's closing lesson. Already linked and correct.
Chores shared in Tenzing's household, his father cleaning, gardening and helping his grandmother cook - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
Tenzing's grandfather's double role, homework and the bus stop at home and social work in the colony - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
Communities managing shared resources by agreed practices, rarely written down, which gave secure access to water, grazing lands and forest produce - this concept's passage.
The halma tradition applied to the Jhabua water crisis, with thousands of trees planted and trenches dug to conserve rainwater - this concept's account. Already linked and correct.
Kamal Parmar's evening classes and free dinner for children who had dropped out or never been to school - this concept's story. Already linked and correct.
How children contribute - this concept says that as children grow up they take on more responsibilities in the home to help other family members, learning through daily practice.
